title: Geometric etale stalks commute with unbounded derived tensor products
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $A$ a commutative ring, and $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$ a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point]. Use the small etale site $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], the constant coefficient sheaf $A_T$ [def-kun-constant-sheaf], and the ordinary unbounded derived category $D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. For $K\in D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ write $K_{\bar t}\in D(A)$ for the result of applying the exact geometric-stalk functor [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] termwise to a representing complex; here $D(A)$ is the derived category of ordinary $A$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Derived tensor on the site is the K-flat construction [def-kun-derived-tensor]; on $D(A)$ it is the total tensor of an ordinary-module K-flat resolution [def-pc-module-kflat-complex]. For all $K,L\in D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ there is a canonical isomorphism in $D(A)$, natural in both variables,
$$
(K\otimes_{A_T}^{\mathbf L}L)_{\bar t}\ \cong\ K_{\bar t}\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}L_{\bar t}.
$$
No boundedness, constructibility, finiteness of $A$, or Tor-amplitude hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0DEN, label lemma-check-K-flat-stalks, clause (1), applied to K-flat representatives of the derived tensor product at the point of the small etale site

proof.text: Write $S$ for the module-valued geometric stalk. By [lem-sfb-etale-stalk-constant-complex-exactness], $S$ preserves acyclic complexes and quasi-isomorphisms, and for every acyclic ordinary $A$-module complex $E$, the constant complex $cE$ is acyclic with a natural chain isomorphism $E\cong S(cE)$. By [lem-sfb-etale-stalk-total-tensor-comparison] write $\theta_{C,D}:S(C\otimes D)\cong SC\otimes SD$ for the normalized natural chain comparison.

source.place: Tag 03EI, label lemma-sheafification-exact; Tag 04EQ, label lemma-stalk-exact-modules, clauses (1) and (3). Constant-germ normalization: etale-cohomology.tex Tag 03PT, label lemma-stalk-exact, clause (2). Applied termwise to unbounded complexes, expanding parent proof step 1.

proof.text: If $P$ is K-flat, then for every acyclic $E$, $cE\otimes_{A_T}P$ is acyclic by [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Its stalk is acyclic by Step 1 and is $E\otimes_A SP$ via $\theta_{cE,P}$ and the constant-germ isomorphism. Thus $SP$ is K-flat by [def-pc-module-kflat-complex]. This tests every acyclic unbounded $E$ and needs no termwise flatness.

source.place: Tag 0DEN, label lemma-check-K-flat-stalks, clause (1); constant-coefficient acyclic test

proof.text: Choose K-flat resolutions with flat terms $P\to C$, $Q\to D$ of representatives of $K,L$ using [lem-kun-flat-resolution-existence]. Their stalk maps are quasi-isomorphisms by Step 1 and their stalks are K-flat by Step 2. By [def-kun-derived-tensor] and [def-pc-module-kflat-complex], the two desired objects are represented by $S(P\otimes Q)$ and $SP\otimes SQ$. Localizing $\theta_{P,Q}$ identifies them.

This comparison is canonical and natural. Changing either K-flat sheaf model along a quasi-isomorphism preserves its tensor with any complex by [lem-kun-derived-tensor-well-defined], using signed symmetry for the other factor; its stalk remains a quasi-isomorphism by Step 1. On modules the fixed stalk factor is K-flat, so its tensor preserves quasi-isomorphisms by [def-pc-module-kflat-complex]. The naturality equation for $\theta$ remains true on inverting these maps, and on composites. More formally, apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] on a small skeleton of the etale site with $R=A_T$: our chosen resolutions have flat terms, so its resolving-subcategory equivalence and unique-extension clause apply to the two bifunctors with values in $D(A)$. They extend $\theta$ and its inverse uniquely, giving a natural isomorphism independent of the resolutions. No boundedness, constructibility, finiteness or Tor-amplitude assumption occurred.
